fields.name: target_locations
fields.description: Read the requested colors in instruction order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cubes' central-axis world [x,y] coordinates using calibration. Keep this requested order fixed. Match each descending cover to the cube underneath. Reconstruct the full horizontal top square from opposing outer edges and corners, and use the intersection of its diagonals as the central-axis landmark. Do not use a bright patch, inset panel, side face, or silhouette centroid. Project that landmark at approximately z=0.06 m only when the cover is resting; do not project its elevated top onto the table plane. For an elevated cover, estimate elevation only when resolvable known-size face geometry or available simultaneous calibrated views actually establish it. Otherwise carry the last reliably localized coordinate rather than projecting onto the resting plane or guessing an elevation correction. Update when reliable geometry becomes visible again. Using the carried locations and tracking_frame to establish initial correspondence, trace each specific container through every available chronological frame before computing its endpoint coordinate. A carried coordinate may predate unresolved airborne motion; use the visual trajectory rather than treating that coordinate as a new spatial identity assignment. At crossings, use continuous motion through intermediate frames, allowing horizontal and vertical image ranking to change; do not transfer identity by nearest previous position, initial slot, or final spatial order alone. Compare successive front frames for residual translation, including during unrelated button motions: reaching a hand waypoint does not imply that covers have settled. Update coordinates after reliably localized translation, including movement during grasping or release. Preserve coordinates when images support stationarity rather than introducing estimation jitter. When localization is unreliable or temporarily occluded, carry the last reliable location without assuming the cover is stationary. Keep tracking later requested targets during button pressing and earlier pickups; use a newly exposed cube to confirm correspondence. Write coordinates to millimetre resolution without implying millimetre measurement accuracy. e.g. [[0.02, -0.18], [0.03, 0.13]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of central-axis world [x,y] coordinates of the containers associated with the requested cube colors, in fixed requested pickup order. Before covering, use the central axes of the corresponding visible cubes. At covering, associate each cube with the container descending over it. Reconstruct the full horizontal top square from its opposing outer edges and corners; use the intersection of its diagonals as the central-axis landmark, not a bright patch, inset panel, side face, or silhouette centroid. Project this landmark at approximately z=0.06 m only for a resting container. For an elevated container, use an elevation estimate only when the images available through this cycle resolve it, for example from resolvable known-size face geometry or simultaneous calibrated views. Otherwise retain the last reliably localized coordinate until reliable geometry becomes visible. Do not derive intermediate coordinates from later cycles or an assumed airborne height. Recheck intermediate annotations using this same landmark and observability convention. Follow each container continuously through every shuffle, allowing its horizontal and vertical image ranking to change at crossings; neither its initial slot nor nearest position alone establishes identity. Check correspondence through successive frames across the episode and correct an erroneous association at its first occurrence and throughout its subsequent values, rather than switching identities at the endpoint. Trace identity through every available chronological frame before localizing the endpoint. Update coordinates after reliably localized translation, including residual exchange motion during button approaches and movement during grasping or release. Reaching a hand waypoint does not establish that containers have settled. Preserve the carried coordinate when images support stationarity; when localization is unreliable or temporarily occluded, retain the last reliable estimate without treating that retention as evidence of stationarity. Write coordinates to millimetre resolution without implying millimetre measurement accuracy. Track only requested targets, including the second target while manipulating the first. Do not assign an unseen color from the final arrangement alone. e.g. [[0.02, -0.18], [0.03, 0.13]]

fields.name: tracking_frame
fields.description: First incorporate any successful lift observed this cycle into pickups_completed. Still-needed targets are entries at zero-based indices greater than or equal to that updated count. Write the latest shown label for which every such remaining target container, or initially uncovered target cube, can be localized unambiguously from the available front and wrist views together. Already successfully lifted targets and distractors need not be visible, even if a completed target has been covered again. The current wrist image may qualify its shared current-frame label; do not assume a wrist image is available for every intermediate motion frame. Partial occlusion is permissible if the available images establish the target centers and correspondence unambiguously. If none qualifies, carry the previous label. At the first cycle write E0. Use this retained keyframe with target_locations to establish identities at the beginning of the next clip. e.g. "E114"
fields.annotation: Latest shown frame label at which all still-needed target containers, or their initially uncovered cubes, can be localized unambiguously using the available front image and, when available for that label, wrist image together. Still-needed targets are entries at zero-based indices greater than or equal to pickups_completed after incorporating the successful lifts observed in this cycle. Use this updated count when evaluating frame eligibility. Already successfully lifted targets and distractors need not be visible, even if a completed target has been covered again. Partial occlusion is permissible when the target centers and correspondence remain unambiguous. Do not assume wrist images exist for intermediate motion frames. Retain the preceding value if no qualifying frame appears in the cycle. This keyframe anchors correspondence between the stored target locations and the next motion clip. Initialize with E0. e.g. "E114"

fields.name: interaction_state
fields.description: Initialize start. Update from observed outcomes and the incoming milestone, not from the action you are about to choose. A completed approach above the robot-left button gives left_hover; its subsequent short close-only motion gives left_ready; descent to button contact gives left_pressed; upward withdrawal gives left_retracted. Apply the analogous right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted milestones at the robot-right button. In particular, arrival with already-closed fingers is still right_hover, not right_ready: the separate short closing action must be observed. Opening after right_retracted gives buttons_finished. Arrival above the next requested container at about 0.20 m gives target_hover; descending and closing around it near 0.063 m gives target_grasped; lifting it clear near 0.20 m gives target_lifted; lowering and opening near 0.07 m gives target_released; withdrawing the empty hand near 0.15 m gives target_cleared. A subsequent approach to the next target returns to target_hover. Retain the incoming state if the expected outcome has not occurred or no control steps executed. e.g. "right_ready"
fields.annotation: Observed interaction milestone, initially start. Button milestones are left_hover, left_ready, left_pressed, left_retracted, right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted, buttons_finished. Hover means the initial approach to that button has finished; ready means the subsequent short closing action has finished, even if the fingers were already closed on arrival. Pressed means the closed hand has descended into button contact; retracted means it has subsequently risen to approximately 0.15 m. buttons_finished means the hand has subsequently opened above the right button. Container milestones are target_hover, target_grasped, target_lifted, target_released, target_cleared. They respectively mean arrival at the selected container's 0.20 m approach, closure around it near 0.063 m, successful lift near 0.20 m, lowering and opening near 0.07 m, and empty-hand withdrawal near 0.15 m. Change only when the corresponding motion outcome is observed, never when its waypoint is selected. e.g. "right_ready"

fields.name: pickups_completed
fields.description: Initialize zero. Increment only when the incoming state is target_grasped and the current clip shows the held requested container successfully raised clear to about 0.20 m, ordinarily revealing its colored cube. Carry the count unchanged in every other situation, including further views of that same held container. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of requested containers successfully lifted in instruction order. Initialize to zero. Increment once when a newly grasped requested container is visibly raised off the table to approximately 0.20 m, exposing its cube. Do not increment for grasp closure, release, withdrawal, or repeated observations of the same lift. e.g. 1

action:
Use the incoming memory together with outcomes visible this cycle to determine the current milestone; write those observations for the next cycle. Begin by locating both buttons and all requested colored cubes. Robot-left is larger world y, appearing on the right of the front image. Estimate geometry with the calibrated cameras, intersecting image rays with the appropriate object surface height rather than treating elevated tops as table points. Use wrist imagery to refine alignment. Do not reuse episode-specific coordinates.

Button rules: Independently localize each button using the center of its circular press surface, intersecting its calibrated image ray with approximately z=0.025 m. Do not use the square base centroid, a table-plane projection, the other button's x coordinate, or the achieved TCP position as its center. Prefer the current calibrated wrist view when the circle is visible. At hover and ready milestones, recompute the button center and command its x,y even if the preceding approach was accepted as complete or the closing action produced little motion. Hover tolerance establishes the milestone, not exact lateral alignment. All references below to the button center mean this visually localized center. From start, approach the robot-left button center at z=0.15 m, orientation [-3.1416,0,0], gripper open. At left_hover, command closure above the same center at z=0.15. At left_ready, descend over that center to commanded z=0.0075, closed. Actual contact may stop the TCP near z=0.024; this counts as contact, not a reason to press deeper. At left_pressed, retract over the localized left-button center to z=0.15 closed. At left_retracted, approach the robot-right button center at z=0.15 with an open command. At right_hover, perform the separate short closing action above the button even when the reported fingers are already closed. At right_ready, descend to z=0.0075 closed. At right_pressed, retract over the localized right-button center to z=0.15 closed. At right_retracted, open above the same button. Continue observing and tracking container exchanges throughout all these motions. Neither a return to the original spatial arrangement nor an unchanged shell appearance resets its hidden color association.

Container rules: After buttons_finished, select target_locations[pickups_completed]. At target_cleared, select that same indexed next uncompleted target. Approach its current center at z=0.20, open, pointing straight down. Choose yaw from its visible square edges so the fingers grasp opposing sides; use an equivalent square-symmetry orientation near zero where possible. At target_hover, descend to the container center at z=0.0633–0.0634 and close. At target_grasped, raise to z=0.20 closed, keeping the grasp orientation and approximately the container center's x,y; a small visual centering correction is appropriate. Fingers stopped around 0.018 m each and a container between them support a successful grasp.

At target_lifted, if more requested pickups remain, lower the held container over its current location to z=0.07 and open, preserving current orientation. At target_released, withdraw vertically with open fingers to approximately z=0.149 before moving laterally to the next target. The completed pickup remains completed even though its cube is covered again. After lifting the final requested container, retain the grasp for automatic success; do not initiate an unnecessary release.

Never issue an exactly identical TCP pose merely to change the gripper. Apply this check only after correcting the nominal close/open waypoint's x,y from visual localization. If the corrected nominal waypoint is still within 2 mm of the current pose, add a small vertical displacement of about 3 mm while retaining the required gripper command. Do not add that offset when lateral correction already makes the waypoint nonidentical. Allow normal motion error when recognizing arrival; do not require exact equality.

If an expected motion did not execute, retain memory milestones and retry with a reachable, nonidentical waypoint. If alignment or grasp is visibly unsuccessful, correct using the current wrist image instead of advancing progress. If a target is temporarily occluded, first withdraw safely to reveal it. If containers are still moving and correspondence needs another observation, a short purposeful wait of 8 control steps may be used to finish tracking before a grasp. Do not guess a hidden color from its original slot, and do not wait without a specific visibility or settling purpose.
